newsitem.title: POLAND: Some Polish firms lose, others gain from floods.
newsitem.headline: Some Polish firms lose, others gain from floods.

text.p: Several listed Polish firms have suffered losses from the current flooding in southern Poland, though others say they are set to gain from contracts as the region dries out, firm officials said on Friday.
Large-cap southern-based firms such as brewer Okocim and paintmaker Polifarb Cieszyn say they have suffered slight setbacks now largely under control.

"Our pipelines supplying solvent were threatened but the situation has been put under control and there's no threat," said Cieszyn security head Zbigniew Kuczera, adding that damages amounted to about one million zlotys.
Production manager Jan Kusiak of Okocim said the brewer had to stop bottling beer for several days when the floodwaters reached its water cleansing station, which will be back in action next week.

Industrial boilermaker Rafako in the badly afflicted town of Raciborz said in a statement on Friday that over 30 percent of its factory buildings were still holding water and staff had begun to repair the damage.
"Floodwater has receded from over 60 percent of the factory buildings. Water supplies and telephone services have been disrupted," the statement said but did not disclose estimated losses.
The Warsaw bourse has suspended trade in both Rafako and electrode maker ZEW, also based in Raciborz.
The two firms were unreachable by telephone on Friday.
Other companies such as construction firms were cheered that at least they could benefit from the damage.
A member of steel trader Stalexport's management office who requested anonymity said the firm had yet to make an estimate of the potential increase in demand for steel goods.
"It can be expected that the firm will enter tenders for supply," the source said.
